text: Mum cancelled on the kids again, an hour before, by text. They were in their coats. I could throw the phone through the window.
Mum cancelled on the kids again and Noor just took her coat off and went upstairs without a word. My heart broke for her.
He read my diary. He actually read it and then quoted it at me in an argument. I have never felt such rage.
Found my old diary from the year Dad died. Read it in the loft until it got dark. Poor kid. Poor fourteen-year-old me.
The council's taking the playground out to build parking. No consultation. I'm writing to every one of them tonight and I'm not being polite.
They took the playground out today. Watched the diggers from the window. Mila learned to swing there. Just a square of mud now.
Jay got the credit for my work in the meeting and didn't correct it. Sat there and let it happen. I'm fuming.
Jay's leaving. Five years sitting next to each other and he's off to Leeds. The desk's going to be very quiet.
The vet lost Pip's results and now she's got to be put through the whole thing again. I was so sharp with the receptionist and I'm not sorry.
Pip's results came back and it's what we feared. Sat on the vet's floor with her head in my lap. We've got a few months.
The driver mounted the kerb and nearly hit Tariq's buggy and then shouted at ME. I'm still shaking with it.
Tariq's last day at nursery. Folded his tiny apron and put it in the memory box. Where does the time go.
Cancelled flight, no refund, 'policy'. Spent two hours on the phone being told no by four different people. I could scream.
Flight cancelled so I'll miss Auntie Rosa's last birthday. She said never mind, love. It's not never mind.
Landlord's put the rent up four hundred a month and called it 'market rate'. The boiler's been broken since January. The nerve.
Packed up the flat today. Eight years. Our first place. The marks on the door frame where we measured Leo.
Dad told my sister she was 'getting fat' at Sunday lunch, in front of her kids. I went outside before I said something I meant.
Dad forgot my sister's name at Sunday lunch. Just for a second. Nobody said anything. Nobody needed to.
The school's changed the uniform again, sixty quid, three weeks' notice. Who do they think pays for this? Livid.
Sami wore the uniform for the last time today. Eleven years, and tomorrow he's a grown-up. Teary at the gate.
They cut the night bus. The one the whole estate uses for shifts. Nobody asked us. Nobody ever asks us.
Last night bus home. The driver, Winston, has done that route since I was a kid. He shook everyone's hand. I had a lump in my throat.
Someone keyed the car in the hospital car park while I was sitting with Mum. Who does that. Who does that outside a hospital.
Sat with Mum in the hospital till they asked me to go. She held my hand and called me by her sister's name. I let her.
Rashid promised he'd be there for the recital and sent a thumbs-up emoji from the pub. A thumbs-up. I'm done being understanding.
Recital tonight and the seat next to me was empty. Amira looked for her dad in the crowd and I watched her face change.
Builder walked off the job with the deposit and his phone's dead. Six grand. I want to find him and I want it to go badly for him.
The extension's finished. Grandad was going to have the downstairs room. We built it for him and he's not here to see it.
My manager said my miscarriage was 'bad timing for the project'. Out loud. To my face. I have never wanted to hit someone before.
The due date would have been today. Nobody remembered. I didn't say. Went for a walk and sat by the river for a long time.
Lena told everyone the thing I told her in confidence. Everyone. I trusted her with that. My hands are shaking.
Lena and I haven't spoken in a year now. I saw her across the market today and she looked away. We used to tell each other everything.
The referee gave it. Gave it! Everyone in the ground saw it wasn't a foul. I shouted things I'm not proud of.
Last game at the old ground before they knock it down. Dad's seat, row M. Stood there after the whistle until the stewards came.
They towed the car from outside my own house because the permit was a day out. A day. Two hundred quid to get it back. Seething.
Sold Dad's car today. The man drove it away and I stood on the pavement. It still smelled of his cigarettes.
Hollie's teacher put her in detention for defending a kid who was being bullied. Defending him! I've asked for a meeting and I will not be calm.
Hollie came home and said nobody sat with her at lunch again. Third day. She said it like it didn't matter. It matters.
The company I've given eleven years to announced redundancies by email at 5pm on a Friday. An email. Cowards, all of them.
Cleared my desk after eleven years. The photo of the team from the first Christmas party. Half of them gone already. Now me.
